key_insight: Scaling ego-centric video data by 100x does improve world-model performance, but the gains are uneven: some capabilities improve much more than others. In particular, the model appears to learn agent behavior more readily than fine-grained object interaction fidelity.
problem_solved: This paper asks whether massive amounts of ego-centric human video are enough to train practical world models, and what they still fail to learn even at large scale.
method: Train and evaluate world models using a very large ego-centric video dataset: 30,000 hours, 1,000+ scene types, and 14,000 contributors.
Measure performance directly on a challenging out-of-distribution benchmark, focusing on agent behavior and object-interaction fidelity instead of opaque downstream proxy metrics.
Compare scaling effects by increasing training data volume by 100x to see which capabilities improve and which remain limited.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, the takeaway is that more video data alone is not a complete solution for world models. Robust physical understanding and interaction modeling likely require better objectives, architectures, or supervision beyond simple scaling.

paper_title: What 30,000 Hours of Ego-centric Video Does Not Teach
paper_authors: Jiahua Dong, Anurag Bagchi, Yash Jangir, Muhammad Zubair Irshad, Sergey Zakharov
